title: namchain engine.schema answer (the node catalogue)
description:
What the engine publishes in answer to {"id":"1","method":"engine.schema"}, and what namchain's own docs/schema.md documents. It is the third leg of the tripod: the rig document (namchain-rig-document.schema.json) says *how a graph is written*; this catalogue says *what a node type is* — what may be added (the palette), what may be turned and in what units over what range (the inspector), and what a parameter name means (the validator). The engine refuses anything its catalogue does not declare.

Source of truth: the emitters in namchain src/daemon/daemon.cpp (param_schema, node_type_schema, macro_type_schema) and the type declarations in src/nodes/builtin.cpp and src/nodes/macros.cpp. Primitives and macros share one array in palette order, told apart by `kind`.

Notes the schema makes explicit:
- A parameter's `default` is null when it is required or a member of a one_of group (publishing the stored zero would be a value no node could be built from).
- `options` and `options_from` are exactly-one-of: fixed options, or values filled from the device's model/IR library (an empty library is an empty `options` list, not an error).
- Bounds that depend on the rig (Nyquist, delay buffer size) are published as null and enforced by the node, not the schema.
- Per-port parameters (`per_port_params`) are runtime, addressed with a port in rig.patch; a rig *file* cannot set one.
- A macro's parameters carry `targets`, the lowered node parameters they drive and how (the transform names).

stereo.description: Declared and refused: the engine is mono end to end, so no stereo block exists to be picked.

channels.description: 1 for every type today; the engine declares the field and refuses anything wider.

optional.description: Inputs are always optional: an unconnected input is legal and bound to silence. Outputs are never optional.

arity.description: For a node whose port count comes from a parameter (nc.split, nc.mix): the parameter, its bounds and its default. Null for a fixed shape.

stateful.description: Explains why bypass keeps the node running rather than removing it.

bypassable.description: The compiler refuses bypass on anything but 1→1; publishing it lets a UI grey the control instead of finding out.

block_delay.description: A scheduling primitive (nc.unit_delay), not a pedal: a palette should leave it out.

value.description: The wire value a document and a patch name.

label.description: The display label; not assumed to be the same string.

id.description: The name a document and a patch use.

kind.description: A count (like a split's outputs) is a number with step 1 and snap; a flag never carries bounds or a step.

unit.description: Hz, dB, ms, samples, %, … or null. What stops a dB knob being wired to a linear gain.

default.description: The *effective* value when the parameter is absent; null for a required parameter or one of a one_of group.

min_inclusive.description: A Q of 0 is excluded rather than clamped.

max.description: Null means unbounded *by the schema* — a bound that depends on the rig (Nyquist, buffer size) is the node's to enforce and name.

step.description: The smallest increment, or null for continuous.

snap.description: What an off-grid value means: rounded to the grid, or refused.

scale.description: Presentation, but presentation the engine knows, so two clients cannot disagree.

rampable.description: A change is ramped inside the node with no recompile — what a slider streams. Without it a change is a structural edit, dual-rendered and crossfaded.

patchable.description: Whether rig.patch may name it at all.

hidden.description: An alias or internal knob a generic inspector leaves out (nc.gain's linear `gain` beside its visible `gain_db`).

required.description: The node cannot be built without it.

one_of.description: A group name for alternatives: nc.delay takes samples OR ms. Giving two members of a group is refused rather than resolved by precedence.

one_of_required.description: Whether at least one member of the group must be present.

options_from.description: For an option whose values live on the device: "models" or "irs". The values are the library's ids — never paths, which a network client may not send. Exactly one of options / options_from is present.

targets.description: Macro parameters only: the lowered node parameters this one drives, and how. Publishing them is what makes 'why did my knob move two nodes' answerable from the daemon.

role.description: The role a client can address with element + role.

category.description: What a palette groups it under. The engine owns these: a type the app cannot name is a type the app cannot offer.

per_port_params.description: Parameters that exist once per port rather than once per node — a mixer's level, mute and polarity per input. Same shape as params, addressed with a port in rig.patch; runtime, not document.

macro.title: macro node type

bypass.description: How the macro bypasses: every lowered role carries the dry signal, or a dry/wet crossfade.

roles.description: The lowered graph's nodes, addressable as element + role.

macro.description: A macro lives in the same array as the primitives, in palette order, and carries the same parameter shape — plus the roles and per-parameter targets that say how it lowers. A client that wants to draw the lowered graph should read rig.get's `lowered` view, not reconstruct it from roles and targets.
